title: Sulfosalicylic Acid Detection of Proteins in Urine of Pregnant Women
author: Fernández Macedo, Cueva Rossel, et al.

steps.title: Collect 24‑hour urine sample
steps.instruction: Obtain a 24‑hour urine collection from each pregnant participant as described in the study.

steps.title: Aliquot urine for test
steps.instruction: Measure 5 mL of the collected urine into a clean test tube.

steps.title: Add sulfosalicylic acid
steps.instruction: Add three drops of 3 % sulfosalicylic acid to the 5 mL urine sample.

steps.title: Observe and interpret turbidity
steps.instruction: Place the tube against a black background and note the appearance: transparent (no proteinuria), cloudy (proteinuria), or dense cloud with granules and agglutination that solidifies >500 mg (massive proteinuria, four crosses, ++++). The degree of turbidity (1–4 crosses) is directly proportional to protein concentration.

steps.title: Record results in SPSS
steps.instruction: Enter each observation into SPSS version 23 for tabulation.

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Using SPSS, calculate sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and generate a receiver‑operating characteristic (ROC) curve; the study reported a sensitivity of 78.3 % and specificity of 47.4 %.
